messages.text: what can you tell me about my current project?

This is an early-stage **portfolio website** for **John Agburu (Illustrator X Graphic Designer)** — a fresh Next.js 16.4.5 app built with pnpm. Here's the rundown:

**Stack**
- Next.js 16.4.5 (App Router) + React 19.3 + TypeScript
- Tailwind CSS v4 (Turbopack), shadcn-style setup (`components.json`, Base UI, CVA, lucide-react)
- Fonts: Space Grotesk + JetBrains Mono; a stark off-white/ink (#eee/#141414) "neo-brutalist" design language with hard 2.5px borders and offset hover shadows

**Structure** (`src/`)
- `app/` — Home (hero with SVG title lockup + greyscale→color portrait hover), plus `/illustrations`, `/projects`, `/journal`, `/other-work`
- `components/` — `Navbar`, `HeroTitleSvg`, `ContactModal`, `ResumeModal`, a `ui/button`
- `context/` — ResumeModalContext + ContactModalContext (persistent modals mounted in root layout, so they're reachable from any page)

**State**
- 6 commits; most recent added the illustrations page with filtering/grid
- **Uncommitted changes**: modified `.gitignore` and `src/app/illustrations/page.tsx`
- Several folders (`hooks`, `data`, `config`, `types`, `sections`) are still empty placeholders, so the illustrations/projects/journal pages likely have stubbed or in-progress content

**Quirks worth knowing**
- AGENTS.md warns this Next.js version has breaking changes vs. typical training data — check `node_modules/next/dist/docs/` before writing code
- Layout is an `h-dvh` locked viewport shell with internal scroll areas (no whole-page scroll on desktop)

Want me to dig into the uncommitted illustrations changes or any specific page?

Set up Ollama so I can build with open models.

Ollama runs open models in two ways:
- Locally, on this computer. Speed depends on the hardware. Large models are slow on a computer without a strong GPU.
- In Ollama's cloud. Cloud models run on Ollama's servers, so they are fast on any computer and need no download. In the CLI, a cloud model name ends in :cloud, for example gemma4:cloud. From code, apps call the API at https://ollama.com.

Before you do anything, learn Ollama from its docs:
- Read the docs index at https://docs.ollama.com/llms.txt.
- Read https://docs.ollama.com/quickstart.md, https://docs.ollama.com/cloud.md, and https://docs.ollama.com/gpu.md.
- If I want to call Ollama from code, read https://docs.ollama.com/api/introduction.md. If this project already uses the OpenAI or Anthropic SDK, also read https://docs.ollama.com/api/openai-compatibility.md or https://docs.ollama.com/api/anthropic-compatibility.md.
- For any other question, search the full docs at https://docs.ollama.com/llms-full.txt.

Then:
1. If the ollama command is not installed, install the Ollama CLI. On macOS or Linux, run: curl -fsSL https://ollama.com/install.sh | sh. On Windows, run in PowerShell: irm https://ollama.com/install.ps1 | iex.
2. Check this computer's GPU and memory against https://docs.ollama.com/gpu.md.
3. Ask me what I want to build.
4. Recommend local models, cloud models, or both for that, and tell me why. If local models would be slow on this computer, recommend cloud models. Cloud models need usage credits or a paid plan.

Do not sign in, create an API key, or use an API key for me. If I choose cloud models, tell me to run ollama signin, or to create a key at https://ollama.com/settings/keys.

All research done — docs read (quickstart, cloud, gpu, opencode integration). Here's the plan:

## Plan: Local Ollama + OpenCode setup

**Your hardware verdict:** RTX 3060 Laptop (6 GB VRAM) + 15.8 GB RAM is a solid local-only rig for *small* agentic models. Anything ~7–8B runs mostly on GPU; bigger will spill into RAM and feel sluggish. Fine for a coding agent; not fine for large models — but you chose local-only, so we stay under that ceiling.

### Steps

1. **Install the Ollama CLI** (Windows, per docs):
   ```powershell
   irm https://ollama.com/install.ps1 | iex
   ```
   Then verify with `ollama --version` (the app/server runs in the background on Windows).

2. **Verify GPU acceleration** — pull a small model, run it, and check `ollama ps` reports the 3060 (not CPU fallback). Your driver and compute 8.6 are both supported per gpu.md.

3. **Pick + pull a local coding model** — OpenCode requires **tool calling** and a **64k+ context window**. For 6 GB VRAM the sweet spot is a ~4–8B model; I'll confirm the current best candidates on `ollama.com/search?c=tools` at execution time (docs example: `qwen3.5`; likely a small/`e2b`-class variant) and configure the 64k context length per docs.ollama.com/context-length.md.

4. **Wire up OpenCode** — you already use opencode in this project, so the cleanest path is the manual setup from the integration doc: add an `ollama` provider (`http://localhost:11434/v1`, `@ai-sdk/openai-compatible`) to your opencode config, listing the pulled model. I'll confirm the exact model ID after the pull. (Alternative: `ollama launch opencode`, which uses an inline config without touching your existing `opencode.json` — I can show both.)

5. **End-to-end test** — run opencode against this repo with a throwaway prompt (e.g. "explain how src/ is organized") and confirm tool calls work against the local model.

**Constraints honored:** no sign-in, no API keys, nothing cloud — localhost:11434 only.

Ready to execute?

Plan mode is still active, so I can't run the installer or make changes yet. The plan stands as presented:

1. Install Ollama CLI (`irm https://ollama.com/install.ps1 | iex`)
2. Verify GPU acceleration (`ollama ps` shows the RTX 3060)
3. Pull a ~4–8B tool-calling model with 64k+ context, sized for 6 GB VRAM

Approve this plan (exit plan mode / hit approve) and I'll execute.

Done — Ollama is fully set up and working with OpenCode. The end-to-end test passed: the model used Glob + Read tools against this repo and correctly identified it.

## Summary

| Component | Status |
|---|---|
| Ollama | v0.40.16 installed (signature-verified installer) |
| GPU | RTX 3060 Laptop detected via CUDA, compute 8.6 |
| Model | `bonsai-2:4b` — 1.6 GB, 256K context, tools/thinking/vision |
| Runtime | **100% GPU**, 3.0 GB total, 65,536 context, flash attention + q8_0 KV cache |
| OpenCode | Ollama provider added to `~/.config/opencode/opencode.jsonc` |

**Usage:** `opencode` then pick `Ollama / Bonsai 2 4B (local)`, or run `opencode run -m "ollama/bonsai-2:4b" "..."`

**Two notes:**
1. Context (64k), flash attention, and KV cache settings are persisted via user environment variables (`OLLAMA_CONTEXT_LENGTH=65536`, `OLLAMA_FLASH_ATTENTION=1`, `OLLAMA_KV_CACHE_TYPE=q8_0`), but the currently running server was started by me with those vars — after a reboot the Ollama app will pick them up automatically.
2. If you ever want more coding quality over speed, `mimo-v2.6:9b` is the upgrade path — but it won't fully fit your 6 GB VRAM, so expect CPU offload and slower runs.

No sign-in, no API keys, nothing cloud — everything runs on your machine as requested.
